memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"Now the LORD had said to Moses, 'I will bring one more plague on Pharaoh and on
Egypt. After that, he will let you go from here, and when he does, he will drive
you out completely.'" - Ex 11:1 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God tells Moses the end is near. Nine plagues have already struck Egypt, and
Pharaoh has hardened himself again and again. Now the tenth is coming, and this
one will break his grip completely.

Notice how God speaks with certainty. He does not say, "I hope this works," or
"Let us try one more time." He says Pharaoh will let the people go, and will
actually drive them out. God is not experimenting with Egypt. He knows the exact
point at which this long struggle will end, and He has known it from the
beginning.

There is comfort here for us. When we are in the middle of a long, hard season,
we usually cannot see the end. Moses had been walking this road for months,
watching Pharaoh promise and then break his promise. But God knew there was a
final chapter, and He knew its date.

The same God who set a limit on Egypt's resistance also set a limit on our
bondage to sin. At the cross, Jesus said, "It is finished" (John 19:30). That
was not a hope. It was a completed work. The deliverance God plans, God
finishes.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where are you tired of waiting for God to act?
2. Does it change anything to know God already sees the end of your struggle?
3. What has God finished for you in Christ that you are still trying to earn?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, I do not always see the end of my difficulties, but You do. Help me to
trust Your timing and rest in the deliverance Jesus has already completed for
me. Amen.
